newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwean industrials trade weaker on Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwean industrials trade weaker on Tuesday.

text.p: Zimbabwe's key industrial index tumbled 166.41 points to close at 10,302.91 on Tuesday, apparently confirming brokers' predictions that the bourse still looked generally weak despite a temporary upsurge resulting from a lower-than-expected inflation figure for May.
Annual inflation fell to 20.7 percent in the year to May from 22.4 percent in April.

"But everyone still thinks inflation will go up next month so there is not likely to be much activity on the stocks," one broker said on Monday, adding that investors were likely to retain a preference for the local money market were interest rates were attractive.

"With the majority of May (company) results already posted, the market looks vulnerable for another test of the 10,000 level. The euphoria which followed the...May inflation figure seems to have expired," another broker said on Tuesday.

Dealers also expect investor interest to be diverted towards the national dairy, Dairibord, which government announced last Thursday it was privatising by selling off 75 percent of its stake in the company to the public.

Counters to trade weaker on Tuesday included blue-chip conglomerate Delta and finance house udc which both shed 15 cents to 1,725 and 275 respectively, while packaging firm Hunyani Warrants was down 20 cents to 80.

Electronics group Apex eased 40 cents to 250, clothing retailer Truworths lost 50 cents to 750, tobacco companies BAT and Rothmans both fell 100 cents to 1,400 and 3,900 and bankers Barclays were the biggest losers of the day, dropping 300 cents to 3,200.

The secondary mining index eased 2.79 points to 951.53, with gold giant Ashanti and coal miners Wankie trading at previous levels while copper house Mhangura lost three cents to 27 and Falgold, another gold producer, put off five cents to 55.
